key_insight: A conductive GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in CuInSe2 bottom cells through ion exchange during co-evaporation, enabling strong passivation and high voltage without requiring extra Cu or Na.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical back-contact passivation strategy for high-efficiency, low-bandgap chalcopyrite solar cells aimed at tandem bottom-cell integration.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap CuInSe2 absorber.
Tested whether added Cu, Na, or oxygen-flow changes were required for GaOx conductivity.
Characterized the GaOx layer structure and its impact on device performance.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: GaOx conductivity appears process- and interface-dependent, so the layer’s crystallinity and formation conditions may need tight control for reproducible scaling.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
